/repos/jdx/demo/pulls/1099.title: feat(age): select a named identity with default_identity or FNOX_AGE_IDENTITY
/repos/jdx/demo/pulls/1099.body:
Shared configs often need a different age identity per machine, for example a separate YubiKey plugged into each computer. Until now the age provider had a single `key_file`, so that meant per-machine config files or wrapper scripts. Requested in [discussion #1095](https://github.com/jdx/fnox/discussions/1095).

The age provider now accepts named identity files and a way to choose one:

```toml
[providers.age]
type = "age"
recipients = ["age1yubikey1...", "age1yubikey1...", "age1..."]
default_identity = "yk1"

[providers.age.identities]
yk1 = "~/.config/fnox/yk1-identity.txt"
yk2 = "~/.config/fnox/yk2-identity.txt"
recovery = "~/.config/fnox/recovery.txt"
```

On a machine with the second YubiKey, `export FNOX_AGE_IDENTITY=yk2` overrides `default_identity`, so one shared `fnox.toml` works everywhere.

- The selected identity replaces `key_file`; paths resolve the same way as `key_file`.
- `FNOX_AGE_KEY` still takes precedence over everything.
- Naming an identity that is not in `identities` is an error that lists the available names.
- Without `identities`, `default_identity` or `FNOX_AGE_IDENTITY`, behavior is unchanged.
- Passphrase-protected identities are not part of this change.

Validation: `mise run test:cargo` passes, including a new unit test for the selection logic. The `FNOX_AGE_IDENTITY` env override is not covered by a test.

nodes.title: feat(age): select a named identity with default_identity or FNOX_AGE_IDENTITY
nodes.body:
Shared configs often need a different age identity per machine, for example a separate YubiKey plugged into each computer. Until now the age provider had a single `key_file`, so that meant per-machine config files or wrapper scripts. Requested in [discussion #1095](https://github.com/jdx/fnox/discussions/1095).

The age provider now accepts named identity files and a way to choose one:

```toml
[providers.age]
type = "age"
recipients = ["age1yubikey1...", "age1yubikey1...", "age1..."]
default_identity = "yk1"

[providers.age.identities]
yk1 = "~/.config/fnox/yk1-identity.txt"
yk2 = "~/.config/fnox/yk2-identity.txt"
recovery = "~/.config/fnox/recovery.txt"
```

On a machine with the second YubiKey, `export FNOX_AGE_IDENTITY=yk2` overrides `default_identity`, so one shared `fnox.toml` works everywhere.

- The selected identity replaces `key_file`; paths resolve the same way as `key_file`.
- `FNOX_AGE_KEY` still takes precedence over everything.
- Naming an identity that is not in `identities` is an error that lists the available names.
- Without `identities`, `default_identity` or `FNOX_AGE_IDENTITY`, behavior is unchanged.
- Passphrase-protected identities are not part of this change.

Validation: `mise run test:cargo` passes, including a new unit test for the selection logic. The `FNOX_AGE_IDENTITY` env override is not covered by a test.

commit.messageHeadline: feat(age): select a named identity with default_identity or FNOX_AGE_IDENTITY

nodes.body:
[P1] **Selected key is ignored**

Named selection replaces `key_file`, but `identity` is still passed unchanged to `new_with_config`. Decryption tries that provider reference before the selected file. A machine switching to a named local key still contacts the old provider and fails without trying the chosen file if that provider is unavailable.

Clear `identity` when a named identity is selected, as the new documentation promises.

[P1] **Inline key override is blocked**

With `FNOX_AGE_IDENTITY=yk2` exported, an age provider without that named entry fails during construction—even when `FNOX_AGE_KEY` contains the correct key. `select_key_file` returns an error before decryption reaches the inline-key check.

Skip named-file selection when `FNOX_AGE_KEY` is set so it retains the promised precedence over every other identity source.

[P1] **Daemon keeps the first identity**

`FNOX_AGE_IDENTITY` is read once per process, but the daemon changes its environment for each request. Non-interactive requests resolve cache misses inside the daemon. After the first request reads this value, later requests with a different identity name still select the first name. Decryption can fail when only the newly selected key matches the requested ciphertext.

Read the variable at selection time instead of keeping it in a `LazyLock`.

**Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

[details: Supported by static analysis]

**Isolate `FNOX_AGE_IDENTITY` in `select_key_file_uses_named_identity`.**

`select_key_file` reads `env::FNOX_AGE_IDENTITY` before it reads `default_identity`. The test does not clear that variable. If a developer or CI job exports it, the default, fallback, and error assertions fail. Clearing the variable inside the test does not help, because the `LazyLock` caches its first read. Pass the environment identity into the selection logic as a parameter, and have the test pass `None` for it.

**Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Heavy lift**

[details: Supported by static analysis]

**Skip the `key_file` resolution when a named identity is selected.**

When `default_identity` or `FNOX_AGE_IDENTITY` selects a named identity, the age provider still resolves `key_file` first. If `key_file` is a secret reference whose provider cannot be resolved, provider creation fails with `ProviderNotConfigured`. The selected identity is never used. `select_key_file` replaces `key_file` only after resolution has already completed, so the replacement cannot prevent this failure. Resolve `key_file` only when no named identity is selected, or make the generated resolver skip `key_file` in that case.
